About the Parliamentary Procedure event

Parliamentary Procedure is a Teamwork event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · speech & presentation.

Ten in-depth lessons for the HOSA Parliamentary Procedure team event (5–8 secondary or postsecondary members), following the 2026–27 guidelines and the National Association of Parliamentarians test plan from Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised In Brief: why have rules, meetings, handling motions, debate, amendments, postponing and referring, changing the group’s mind, voting and elections, bylaws and other rules, enforcing and suspending rules and officers and committees. Also covers writing previous minutes and reports, the 15-minute preparation and the 10-minute secret-topic meeting judged on a 162-point rubric. Includes precedence, table-of-rules, vote-threshold and scripting drills.

Sample Parliamentary Procedure questions

1. If an organization’s bylaws do not set a quorum, what is the quorum under Robert’s Rules?

  1. Any number of members present
  2. Two-thirds of the membership
  3. Ten members
  4. A majority of the entire membership
Show answer

D. A majority of the entire membership

The quorum is the minimum number needed to do business. Organizations usually set a lower number in their bylaws.

2. How does a member obtain the floor to speak?

  1. Rises and waits to be recognized
  2. Speaks out whenever there is a pause
  3. Raises a hand without waiting
  4. Writes a note to the secretary
Show answer

A. Rises and waits to be recognized

Only the member recognized by the chair may speak, which keeps the meeting orderly.

3. Which is a privileged motion?

  1. Amend
  2. Postpone indefinitely
  3. Recess
  4. Refer to a committee
Show answer

C. Recess

Privileged motions deal with urgent matters unrelated to pending business: fix the time to adjourn, adjourn, recess, question of privilege and call for the orders of the day.
